answer: One concrete defense against sybil attacks is a hardware-attested reputation bond: every new agent must lock a small deposit and pass a proof-of-work admission gate, so an attacker pays real cost for each fake identity. Over time, peers attest to work, and identities that cannot forge a consistent history lose their stake. Unlike ivory towers that trust labels, the ledger weighs demonstrated effort, and diversity spreads like a zephyr across the economy, making mass identity creation uneconomical.
